theme: Positioning the framework against other strategy tools
why_it_matters: The largest single cluster in the corpus, and practitioners nearly always arrive holding one of these tools. An agent that cannot say what a scorecard or an objectives-and-key-results set has and has not settled will argue about the tool instead of finding the missing choice.
note: Undeclared before the corpus was indexed. Now modelled, though 15 posts could support considerably more depth.

theme: How the answers change by setting - startup, fragmented, monopoly, social sector, university, B2B, scale
why_it_matters: The second largest cluster. Applying a rubric written for a branded commercial business to any of these settings produces confident false findings, which cost more credibility than saying nothing.
note: Undeclared before indexing. Each named setting could justify its own conditional test set.

theme: Who does strategy, and what makes someone good at it
why_it_matters: A substantial cluster about the practitioner rather than the artefact - the chief strategy officer's remit, whether a finance chief can be strategic, what distinguishes a strategist from a technocrat, how to train a novice, and how to work for someone who is not one. The graph assesses strategies and says nothing about the people making them.
note: Closed by adding pillar:practitioner (12th pillar, order 15, between classifying the artefact and working the cascade). This is the one theme that is not about the strategy artefact but about the person making it, so it needed its own pillar rather than being folded into an existing one. Remaining depth: the strategy-function remit and capability-building concepts carry no test yet.

theme: The strategy/execution split as the defect rather than the remedy
why_it_matters: 'The strategy is right, execution failed' is the single most common way a strategy escapes examination. Without a named treatment, the agent has no way to challenge it.
note: Undeclared before indexing.

theme: What AI changes about strategy practice
why_it_matters: Eight posts, several among the most recent in the corpus. Also bears on this repository's own premise: what an assistant should and should not do in strategy work.
note: I rated this medium before indexing. Eight posts, trending recent, means it should have been high.

theme: Corporate strategy across a portfolio of businesses
why_it_matters: The cascade as modelled assumes a single business in an arena. A multi-business parent faces a distinct question - why these businesses are worth owning together - which the original test set did not reach.
note: Declared before indexing and confirmed by it - 7 dedicated posts.

theme: Design thinking and where possibilities come from
why_it_matters: Teams evaluate options competently and generate them badly. Without this, the agent can test a choice set but cannot notice that the choice set is the binding constraint.
note: Declared as thin before indexing and confirmed - 8 posts. Still thinner in the graph than the corpus warrants.

theme: Reliability versus validity, and analytics that wreck strategy
why_it_matters: A consistent process applied to a strategic question yields defensible wrong answers, and its consistency is what makes them hard to challenge. Distinct from the faux-rigour treatment already present.
note: Undeclared before indexing; the reliability/validity distinction was the specific thing missing.

theme: Strategy without a commercial market
why_it_matters: This was a rubric bug, not only a missing topic: several tests were phrased in terms of buying at a price, so a sound social-sector, public or membership strategy failed test:customer_action_named for the wrong reason.
note: Rubric bug now fixed: test:customer_action_named accepts a non-purchase exchange and carries a context_note. The corpus confirms the series addresses this directly.

theme: Whether an organisation can pursue cost and differentiation together
why_it_matters: A second rubric risk found by indexing. The original test asserted a hard either/or, but the corpus treats the question with more nuance - a distinctive position still has to be delivered at a cost its premium can carry. An over-rigid test would mark a coherent strategy as confused.
note: The test still requires a primary route to be chosen, which is right; the added concept and question give the agent the coherent version of 'both' so it does not over-reject.

theme: Specific competitive mechanics - substitutes, first-mover costs, hold-up, monopolist behaviour, races to the bottom
why_it_matters: pillar:competition covers response and imitation generically. These named mechanics are what practitioners actually face, and each implies a different must-be-true.
note: Undeclared before indexing.

theme: Pay for performance, single-point accountability and how responsibility is assigned
why_it_matters: pillar:management_systems covers measures and ownership but treats incentive design as unproblematic, where the corpus argues the standard approaches actively work against strategy.
note: Undeclared before indexing. Note the tension with test:choices_have_owners, which assumes named single owners are straightforwardly good.

theme: Strategy and time - horizons, discontinuity, exploration versus exploitation
why_it_matters: The graph is largely timeless. When a choice must be made, how long it should hold, and how to balance exploiting the current position against exploring the next are all unmodelled.
note: Undeclared before indexing.

theme: Communicating a strategy and getting genuine buy-in
why_it_matters: pillar:adoption tests whether a strategy is sayable and cascaded, but not how agreement is actually won or why shared vocabulary breaks down.
note: Undeclared before indexing.

theme: Two-sided markets, platforms and network effects
why_it_matters: Where-to-Play and How-to-Win behave differently when the customer set is two populations that value each other. No test distinguishes a platform strategy from a linear one.
note: Declared before indexing and confirmed, though with fewer dedicated posts than expected.

theme: Brand as an expression of the promise
why_it_matters: concept:pttc covers the promise; nothing covers how brand choices reinforce or contradict it, or the claim that marketing and strategy are one discipline.
note: Declared before indexing and confirmed.

theme: The board's role in strategy
why_it_matters: Three dedicated posts, including how management should use a board rather than merely report to it. concept:choice_chartering stops at the executive layer.
note: I rated this low before indexing; three dedicated posts makes it medium.

theme: Sustainability and corporate purpose as strategic choices
why_it_matters: Usually arrives as an additive priority list, which trap:initiative_list describes but which practitioners will not recognise as the same thing without a named treatment. The corpus also argues promise should take precedence over purpose.
note: I rated this low before indexing; four posts plus the promise-over-purpose argument makes it medium.

theme: Segmentation, identifiability and the problem with averages
why_it_matters: concept:behavioural_segments requires segments to be behavioural but says nothing about whether a segment can actually be identified and reached, which is what makes a segmentation usable.
note: Undeclared before indexing.

theme: Talent and HR as a functional strategy
why_it_matters: Talent is the function where capability claims most often go to die.
note: I rated this medium before indexing. One dedicated post means low.

theme: Strategy under binding regulatory or policy constraint
why_it_matters: In regulated arenas the regulator is a party whose behaviour the strategy depends on.
note: I rated this medium before indexing. The corpus addresses it once, on tariffs, so low.

theme: Strategy under cost pressure and disruption
why_it_matters: Cost cutting under pressure is the moment a strategy quietly becomes neither low cost nor differentiated.
note: I rated this medium before indexing. Thinner than expected in the corpus.

theme: Pricing as a strategy choice rather than a finance exercise
why_it_matters: Price now appears in test:customer_action_named as part of the success condition, which is where the corpus puts it.
note: I rated this HIGH before indexing, on the assumption that a practitioner series would treat pricing directly. Zero dedicated posts. That rating came from my own priors about practitioner pain, not from this corpus.

theme: Acquisitions as a strategic choice
why_it_matters: Acquisition remains a route for closing a capability gap, and slot:capability_gaps already accepts 'buy' as an option.
note: I rated this HIGH before indexing and claimed it was 'a recurring subject in the series'. Zero dedicated posts across 288. That claim was fabricated inference, and this entry stands as the record of it.

theme: Shareholder value maximisation versus customer-first capitalism
why_it_matters: It bears on pillar:winning_aspiration - whose win is being defined - so it would matter if the corpus developed it.
note: I rated this HIGH before indexing, describing it as 'a substantial strand of the author's work'. That is true of the author's books and journal articles but not of this Substack series, which touches it once. A gap register must be scoped to the corpus it claims to cover.

theme: Applying the cascade to a career or an individual
why_it_matters: Out of scope for an enterprise coaching agent, recorded so the omission stays deliberate.
note: The corpus covers this more than I assumed when I first excluded it - four posts. Still excluded, but now by choice against known evidence rather than by guess.
